title: Large values of exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
summary: In 1977 Montgomery and Vaughan gave tight bounds for exponential sums of the form $\sum_{n\leq x}f(n)e(nα)$ where $f$ is a $1$-bounded multiplicative function and $α\in\mathbb R$, close to the conjectured $\ll \frac{x}{\sqrt{q}}+ \frac{x}{\log x}$ where $α$ is best approximated by $|α-a/q|\leq 1/(qx)$, showing their results to be ``best-possible'' by observing that the first part of their bound is more-or-less attained when $f(n)=χ(n), α=\frac aq$ where $χ$ is a primitive character mod $q$, and the second part when $f(p)=e(-αp)$ for all large primes $p$.
